messages:
maria: heads-up: I ran into an ambiguous routing case in staging — two different override rules both match the same incoming request and we fall back to whichever rule was loaded last. can we define a deterministic tiebreaker and surface it in the Console?

maria: repro (short):
1) route /v1/generate base -> default model m-small
2) override A: header matcher `x-ro-priority: high` -> model m-large
3) override B: header matcher `x-ro-env: prod` -> model m-xlarge
request has both headers. currently we pick B because it was created later. not great.

ashok: +1. we should have a clear precedence: exact path > header count > header specificity > creation time as last resort.

jon: what do you mean by header specificity? example?

ashok: header specificity = whether matcher is exact vs regex or list. e.g. `x-ro-env: prod` vs `x-ro-env: prod|stg` — exact literal should beat a regex/list.

kevin: can we just require an explicit priority field on overrides? then Console can expose a numeric rank and linter can complain if two matches tie. simpler.

lia: I like explicit priority, but default should be deterministic for existing users. adding a new required field would be breaking. make it optional and documented.

maria: proposal: add optional `priority` integer on override (higher = wins). if missing, compute precedence: 1) path specificity, 2) number of matchers (more matchers wins), 3) matcher specificity score (literal>list>regex), 4) creation_ts.

jon: sounds reasonable. we should also add a Console hint panel that shows "Why this override was selected" with the precedence breakdown for the request. helps debuggability.

kevin: agree. and add a lint rule: warn when two active overrides can both match identical header sets and neither has priority. maybe suggest adding `priority` or tightening matchers.

lia: small UX note: Console should let you drag reorder overrides to set priority and persist that as the `priority` field. non-destructive UI.

maria: +1 on drag-to-rank. Also we need schema and server-side validation:
- YAML/JSON schema update to accept `priority` integer >=0
- validation error if duplicate priority values in same route? or allow same and fallback to computed rules?

ashok: prefer allowing duplicates but warn. if duplicates exist and both match, fallback to computed precedence then creation_ts. explicit priority should mostly be unique in practice.

jon: on the linter/tests: add unit tests covering all combos (literal vs regex, different matcher counts, identical matchers with different creation times) plus an integration test that hits the Console "why chosen" endpoint showing breakdown.

deploy-bot: CI lint check: routing-schema.json updated? Not found. Please add schema bump to PR.

maria: noted — I'll draft a minimal schema patch and the Console hint mock. will open PR with tests. thanks all :pray:

kevin: TL;DR: add optional `priority`, deterministic fallback rules, Console "why this override" panel, and linter warnings. good enough to move forward?

lia: yes. please include migration notes in the PR (how existing routes behave).

maria: will do. target PR today, tests tomorrow.

jon: if you want me to pair on the Console panel mock, ping me.

maria: thanks — will ping in thread.
